bottom_line: Prices are still rising too fast. The Fed's favorite inflation measure hit 3.8% in October, so the Fed (the people who set interest rates) looks set to raise rates in December. Borrowing is getting more expensive at the same moment AI stocks are getting hammered.

stories.title: Inflation hot, Fed ready to hike
stories.real: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose to 3.8% in October, and inflation stayed high even though gas prices dropped. Economic growth for the third quarter was also revised sharply higher, so the Fed has little reason to wait, and a December rate hike now looks close to locked in.
stories.you: Loans, credit cards and mortgages can get more expensive when the Fed raises rates, while everyday prices keep climbing.

stories.title: AI stocks get crushed
stories.real: Tech stocks sold off hard on fears about AI spending and debt. The Nasdaq fell almost 4% at one point, Nvidia sank 7%, and the Nasdaq 100 is on pace to enter a bear market (down 20% from its high). Scared money ran to Treasuries (US government bonds), which pushed their yields down.

stories.title: Anthropic slides below IPO price
stories.real: Anthropic, the AI company that just went public, has dropped below its IPO price (the price it first sold shares at) and is hovering around a $1 trillion value. Analysts are defending its business with big companies, but the slide is testing how much people still trust the AI trade.
stories.you: A brand-new stock can fall right after it lists, even a famous one.

stories.title: Nvidia's CEO scandal and politics
stories.real: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after reported affairs, then was brought back after pressure from Trump. The board now faces an investigation and a shareholder lawsuit. Records also show Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, and he says it's 'not too late' for the US to take a stake in Nvidia.
stories.you: When one giant company is this tied to one person and to politics, its stock can swing wildly, and so can the funds that hold it.

stories.real: The US proposed new tariffs (taxes on imported goods) on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU. Analysts warn tariffs push prices up no matter how they're put in place, and that adds to the case for higher rates.
stories.you: Imported goods could cost more on top of prices that are already rising.
